table.name: battle
table.purpose: Battles of the Bulgarian–Latin Empire (Fourth Crusade aftermath) wars, c. 1205–1235: each row is one battle/siege with its date, opposing leaders, and outcome. Referenced by death and ship tables.

col_001.name: battle_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate integer identifier for each battle. Referenced by death and ship tables.

col_002.name: battle_name
col_002.description: Name of the battle or siege (e.g. Battle of Adrianople, Siege of Constantinople).

col_003.name: battle_date
col_003.description: Date of the battle, stored as free text with mixed precision (full day, month-year, or year only), e.g. '14 April 1205', 'June 1205', '1235'.

col_004.name: bulgarian_leader
col_004.description: Leader of the Bulgarian side: a Bulgarian tsar (Kaloyan, Boril, Ivan Asen II) or 'Unknown'.

col_005.name: latin_leader
col_005.description: Leader of the Latin Empire (Crusader) side: Latin emperors or nobles (Baldwin I, Henry I, John of Brienne, Boniface of Montferrat, Thierry de Termond) or 'Unknown'.

col_006.name: outcome
col_006.description: Result of the battle: 'Bulgarian victory', 'Latin victory', or 'Two Year Truce'.

table.name: death
table.purpose: Records of death incidents, each row an incident at a location in India (district, state) with counts of casualties. The joins to 'ship' and 'battle' (naval/historical battle names) are inconsistent with the location data and appear spurious; the table is most plausibly a record of violent incidents (e.g., insurgent/encounter deaths) by district, with counts of deaths and injuries. Evidence is thin (13 rows), so overall meaning is tentative.

col_002.name: id
col_002.description: Primary key; unique sequential integer 1-13 identifying each death incident row.

col_003.name: location
col_003.description: Location of the incident as 'district, state' (e.g., 'Dantewada, Chhattisgarh', 'East Champaran, Bihar'), all in eastern/central India. Dantewada appears 5 times.

col_004.name: deaths
col_004.description: Count of deaths in the incident, 0-29, mostly small (median 3, five rows with 0). Plausibly the number of people killed; could alternatively be another casualty count, but 'deaths' fits the table name.

col_005.name: injuries
col_005.description: Small count 0-9, zero in 11 of 13 rows. Likely a secondary casualty count such as number injured; too little evidence to be sure.

table.name: ship
table.purpose: A register of ships (mostly brigs) and their fates — each row is one ship, with its name, rig/armament, location of loss, and outcome (captured, sank, scuttled, wrecked). The ships appear to be lost or taken in naval engagements, since col_001 points to a battle table. The exact historical scope is unclear because the referenced lookup data is inconsistent with the ship data (see col_001).

col_001.name: battle_id
col_001.description: Reference to the battle or engagement in which the ship was lost; joins many ships to one battle (battle.col_001). The battle table documents medieval Balkan battles (c. 1205-1235), which is inconsistent with these 18th/19th-century naval brigs, so the precise identity of the referenced entity remains uncertain; only the many-to-one battle reference is supported.

col_002.name: ship_id
col_002.description: Primary key of the ship table; unique integer identifier for each ship row. Referenced by death.col_001.

col_003.name: ship_name
col_003.description: Name of the ship (e.g. 'HMS Avon', 'Lettice', 'Mary', 'Bacchus', 'Bon Accord', 'Three Brothers', 'HMS Atalanta'). Unique per row.

col_005.name: ship_type
col_005.description: Rig/type and armament of the vessel: 'Brig' (5 rows), '18-gun Brig', '8 gun Brig'. Describes the ship class, including gun count where known.

col_006.name: loss_location
col_006.description: Sea area where the ship was lost or captured: 'English Channel' (5), 'Mid-Atlantic', 'SW Approaches'.
